task.description: Independently re-verify REQ-269's marker insertion across 13 lib/letflow/design/ files, with particular scrutiny on the blockquote-marker edge case in req151.

result.note: All 7 checks independently re-derived, none trusted from DOC-UPDATER's handoff. (1) git diff 0231f7f5..HEAD --stat: exactly the 13 named files plus this run's own step-00/step-02 handoff jsons, 71 insertions(+), 0 deletions -- no other file, no deletion. (2) Per-file marker counts via `grep -c 'PROVENANCE (historical, not current decision authority):'`: req083=10, req085=5, req109=20, req135=11, req137=7, req148=2, req151=2, req152=1, req154=1, req157=4, req158=5, req163=2, req171=1 -- sum=71, matches claim exactly. (3) `git diff 0231f7f5..HEAD -- <each file> | grep -E '^[+-]' | grep -v PROVENANCE` returned empty for all 13 files: every changed line in every file is exclusively an added PROVENANCE line, nothing else added or removed -- strongest possible confirmation of byte-identical citation text (also independently confirmed via sorted `grep '\.zig'` before/after per file, all identical). (4) req151-lua-sandbox.md blockquote case scrutinized directly: the `> PROVENANCE (historical, not current decision authority):` line at (current) line 267 sits inside an unbroken `> `-prefixed blockquote spanning lines 258-282, immediately above the '(b) `jit`, `ffi`, and `bit`...stdlib.zig' paragraph which is the actual .zig-carrying unit -- confirmed the citation is genuinely inside the blockquote, the marker is correctly `> `-prefixed (not breaking the quote into two blocks), and it precedes only that paragraph, not the whole quote. This is judged a defensible mechanical extension, not an unauthorized new convention: it is structurally identical in kind to the design doc's own ISS-0510 YAML-comment-line amendment (§2) -- same marker text verbatim, prefix added only because the surrounding syntax (Markdown blockquote / YAML comment) would otherwise be corrupted by a bare line, and greppability is preserved either way since grep matches the string regardless of a leading '> ' or '#'. However, strictly speaking neither §2's enumerated four unit shapes nor its amendments literally list 'blockquote line' as a shape -- DOC-UPDATER applied the same underlying principle by analogy rather than finding it pre-authorized verbatim. This is flagged as a minor process note (not a blocking finding): recommend REQ-237's design doc get a short follow-up amendment (mirroring the ISS-0510 note) formally naming the blockquote-prefix shape, so future DOC-UPDATER turns don't have to re-derive the same by-analogy judgment call file by file. Does not block PASS here since the applied instance is correct and consistent with precedent. (5) `grep -rnE 'unlike R-Co|deliberately diverges|diverges from R-Co'` re-run against base 0231f7f5 and HEAD for all 13 files: only req109-variable-schemas.md matches, 2 lines both times, text byte-identical ('It diverges from R-Co, which validates every key...' and the OQ-1 heading), only line numbers shifted (360->367, 709->723) purely from markers inserted earlier in the same file -- matches DOC-UPDATER's claim exactly. (6) `git diff main..HEAD -- CLAUDE.md README.md docs/migration/README.md` empty; `git diff 0231f7f5..HEAD --stat -- lib/letflow/design/` shows only the 13 named files (71 insertions, 0 deletions) -- no other design file touched. (7) All 13 files' first lines are Markdown `#`/`###` headings, no YAML frontmatter (`---` block) in any of them. No discrepancies found anywhere; DOC-UPDATER's reported counts and diff-scope claims all independently reproduced exactly.
